To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the major risk factors for coronary heart disease and stroke are high blood pressure, cigarette smoking, and high cholesterol levels, and that these factors can be modified by appropriate interventions.

(1) high blood pressure is a major risk factor for stroke and coronary heart disease; (2) antihypertensives are effective in preventing these diseases; (3) multifactorial intervention is more effective than unifactorial treatment; (4) the benefits of multifactorial intervention are greatest among persons at high risk for stroke and coronary events; and (5) the benefits of antihypertension are greatest when blood pressure is lowered to normal.

multifactorial interventions, which are based on a combination of unifactorially effective treatments and which are directed at persons who have a high risk of coronary heart disease and/or stroke, can reduce the incidence of these two diseases.
